cites.quote: A cancelled appointment always has a reason of up to 300 characters
today it is shown only on the appointment's own page.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason
Medical history appears only on the patient's own page, never in lists
A cancellation reason is at most 300 characters; the list must handle any reason up to that length.

findings.suggested_fix: Keep 300 characters as context (C1) and restate REQ-16 as a checkable list behaviour, e.g. a 300-character reason shows the first 60 characters plus "…" without breaking the row; or drop it as covered by REQ-5.
findings.text: REQ-16 is compound and partly untestable: it states a data rule (at most 300 characters) and a vague list behaviour ('must handle any reason') with no condition a tester could check.

cites.quote: The column follows the list's status filter, date range and paging.

findings.suggested_fix: Split into one REQ per list control, or state one testable condition covering all three.
findings.text: REQ-8 bundles three behaviours (status filter, date range, paging) in one requirement.

cites.quote: Sorting or searching the list by cancellation reason.
Changing how a reason is entered, its length limit, or which statuses have one.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a reason to each, e.g. 'not asked by HMS-33'.
findings.text: Two Out-of-scope entries give no reason for exclusion.

cites.quote: REQ-1 to REQ-15: ticket acceptance criteria 1 to 8, one behaviour each.

findings.suggested_fix: List which criterion each REQ comes from, and mark REQ-6 and REQ-9 as derived.
findings.text: The Known section says REQ-1 to REQ-15 map to criteria 1-8 'one behaviour each', but then lists REQ-6 and REQ-9 as derived, so the mapping is inconsistent.

cites.quote: Medical history appears only on the patient's own page, never in lists, the dashboard or logs.
A cancelled appointment always has a reason of up to 300 characters, entered when it is cancelled;

findings.suggested_fix: Add a note or assumption that reasons are not medical history, citing both sides, so later steps can confirm it.
findings.text: The cancellation reason is free text, and REQ-14 only covers adding the medical history field. Staff could type medical details into a reason, which would then show in a list. The artifact does not mention this against the data-protection rule.

rubric_items.reason: All 8 acceptance criteria and the 300-character fact map to REQ-1..REQ-16; out-of-scope items are listed.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable; REQ-16 mixes a data limit with a vague list-handling behaviour, and REQ-8 bundles three behaviours.
Every known REQ cites the ticket line or baseline/glossary it comes from; derived REQ-6 and REQ-9 explain their basis. Nothing invented.
No direct clash with the baseline; the free-text reason vs the no-medical-history-in-lists rule is not discussed.
No questions asked; the ticket gives values for every criterion, so none were needed.
Plain wording; glossary status terms used consistently.
